attempts.summary: Published node2's port-8080 app to node3 through node1 (VyOS) via a new private link and DNAT, without exposing the rest of the private network. Set up a private 10.50.50.0/24 subnet on node1 eth1 (10.50.50.254) and node2 eth1 (10.50.50.11), moved the app to bind only on the private address (added a persistent socat-based OpenRC service), added a VyOS destination-NAT rule forwarding node1 eth0:8080 to 10.50.50.11:8080, and a default-deny forward firewall with a rule scoped only to that flow. Fixed an asymmetric-routing issue (node2's eth0 also sits on the shared 10.100.22.0/24 network, so replies bypassed node1) by adding a persistent host route on node2 sending node3-bound traffic back via node1's private IP. Verified node3 can reach the app on port 8080 through node1 but cannot reach node2's private IP or any other private-network resource directly. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of config, service, and connectivity.
